questions.text:
Which of the following languages is/are regular?
[latex]L_{1}:\{wxw^{R}|w,x \in \{a,b\}^{*} \; and \; |w|,|x| \gt 0 \}, w^{R}[/latex] is the reverse of string w
[latex]L_{2}:\{a^{n}b^{m}|m\neq n \; and \; m,n\geq 0\}[/latex]
[latex]L_{3}:\{a^{p}b^{q}c^{r}|p,q,r\geq 0\}[/latex]
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- L1: since x can be anything, it is enough that the first and last symbols match (w of length 1). L1 = a(a+b)+a + b(a+b)+b [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] regular.
- L2: [latex]a^nb^m[/latex] with [latex]m\ne n[/latex] needs counting [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not regular.
- L3 = a*b*c* [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] regular.

Answer: L1 and L3 only

questions.text: The number of states in the minimal deterministic finite automaton corresponding to the regular expression (0+1)*(10) is __________.
questions.solution:
Language: strings ending in "10". States needed: no progress, last symbol 1, last two symbols 10 (accepting).

These are all distinguishable, so the minimal DFA has 3 states.

Answer: 3

questions.text:
Consider the following statements.
I. The complement of every Turing decidable language is Turing decidable
II. There exists some language which is in NP but is not Turing decidable
III. If L is a language in NP, L is Turing decidable

Which of the above statements is/are true?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: decidable languages are closed under complement [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- II: every NP language is decided by a (time-bounded) Turing machine [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False
- III: same reason [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True

Answer: Only I and III

questions.text:
Consider the NPDA [latex]\langle Q=\{q_{0},q_{1},q_{2}\},[/latex] [latex]\Sigma =\{0,1\},[/latex] [latex]\Gamma =\{0,1,\perp \},\delta ,q_{0},\perp ,[/latex] [latex]F=\{q_{2}\} \rangle[/latex], where (as per usual convention) Q is the set of states, [latex]\Sigma[/latex] is the input alphabet, [latex]\Gamma[/latex] is the stack alphabet, [latex]\delta[/latex] is the state transition function, [latex]q_{0}[/latex] is the initial state, [latex]\perp[/latex] is the initial stack symbol, and [latex]F[/latex] is the set of accepting states. The state transition is as follows:

Which one of the following sequences must follow the string 101100 so that the overall string is accepted by the automaton?
questions.solution:
q0 pushes the input. It moves to q1 on one symbol or [latex]\epsilon[/latex] (an optional middle symbol). In q1, a 0 pops a 1 and a 1 pops a 0, so the second half must be the complement of the first half reversed.

Total length 6 + 5 = 11, so w = 10110 and the middle symbol is 0.
Reverse of w = 01101, complement = 10010.

Answer: 10010

questions.text: Consider the DFAs M and N given above. The number of states in a minimal DFA that accepts the language L(M)[latex]\cap[/latex] L(N) is___________
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- M accepts strings ending with a.
- N accepts strings ending with b.

No string can end with both, so [latex]L(M)\cap L(N)=\emptyset[/latex]. The minimal DFA has a single non-accepting state.

Answer: 1
